# BOOK 1 of 2: Polly the Pagan: Her Lost Love Letters (Isabel Anderson, 1922; foreword by Basil King)

## Framing (Editor's note, "The Lost Lady")
- Isabel Anderson (narrator/editor) is an army nurse on Good Friday night 1918 in Paris (Grande Hotel du Nord). An air raid hits. A blonde American woman with blue eyes and one arm in a sling, golden hair, asks for help dressing and hands Anderson a small morocco bag, then runs back for something. Anderson goes to the cellar; a bomb strikes; the woman never appears. Anderson takes the bag to the front.
- Bag contents: papers, a clipping about a mysterious Russian Prince "Kosloff," a Red Cross badge, secret service insignia, letters with nicknames.
- Three replies to her ads in Paris papers: (1) Captain T----F---- (Café Russe, Rue des Capuchins, woman with big blonde foreigner called Prince; suspected American secret service vs German spy); (2) Y.M.C.A. worker S----B---- (woman on Amiens–Paris train, carried black morocco bag, dressed as Salvation Army girl); (3) clerk Joseph M---- at Grande Hotel du Nord (woman arrived Good Friday evening, arm in sling, papers destroyed in fire).
- Anderson publishes extracts with changes; "Polly" possibly the owner.

## Part I: Doings and Misdoings of Polly the Pagan
Polly = twenty-year-old American girl (footnote: "Written at the age of twenty. I. A."). Twin brother **Checkers** (Brother; slang-speaking; cart and pony on the Campagna). Aunt (widowed; reddish hair; "Cart Horse"; Uncle John once; calls Polly "Pliny" later). Maid **Louisa** (Italian contadina; calls Aunt "he", Checkers "she", Polly "it"). Friend **Sybil** (black hair, blue eyes, smokes, later engaged to Checkers). Mockingbird Cæsar. Terrace garden in Rome palazzo.

Key characters:
- **Prince Boris** (Russian, "Cossack," blonde moustache, Oriental cane, broken English, calls Polly "Hummingbird", "Cleopatra girl", "Pagan"). Met on steamer *Cleopatra*: she entered his stateroom by mistake in rainbow negligée with wing sleeves (stateroom 26 thought). Knob fell off door. He proposes in Rome (Polly refused). Gives gifts; later prince is revealed as forger/thief/spy.
- **A. D.** (American Diplomat, American Secretary, dark, slender, clean-shaven; "love-proof"; devoted later to Polly; faithful servant **Gilet**). Polly calls him "Dip". Gave her gold pen, pin (baby Leo), pocket case, silver gondola, silver broom, pearl necklace, engagement ring at Christmas.
- **Mona Lisa** / divorcée, gray cat's eyes, Mona Lisa smile; A. D.'s rival; threatened Polly; later married Peppi.
- **Peppi** (Don Peppi; artist, dark, wild hair; painted Aunt's portrait; married Mona Lisa in May).
- **Captain Carlo** (Don Carlo; dashing Italian officer; poor; went to South Africa; gardener's daughter jealous, wrote anonymous letter signed "Brown Eyes" warning Polly).
- **Pittsburgo** (big wild-eyed American from Pittsburg; shot himself in Rome in front of portrait of Italian singer).
- **Marquis Gonzaga** (Spanish diplomat; flashing black eyes; kissed Polly at dinner; proposed by letter; later duel with Boris; to marry Spanish Countess cousin).
- **Jonkheer Jan** (Dutch Secretary, tall, thin, blonde). **Lord Ronald Charlton** (British Secretary, pale, thin, coins hobby; ill; died; Polly's "Dip" friend). **Turkish Ambassador "Pan"** (red fez, jewelled rings, "Pan"). **Easthope** (London lodgings Half Moon Street). **Rossi** (artist). **Gilet** (A. D.'s man).

Chronology of Part I:
- Jan: steamer *Cleopatra* from Egypt; Boris letters ("Mademoiselle Hummingbird", "Avis").
- Rome, roof garden on palazzo; Louisa brings letter; Boris "My leetle Pagan".
- Polly throws rose/violets to Boris who followed her; Boris introduced by American Secretary (A. D.).
- Dinner at Grand Hotel with Captain Carlo; A. D. gives Polly lift (carriage fails); Duchess Sermoneta's dance.
- Pittsburgo's dinner; Marquis kisses Polly at table after she pricks him with pin.
- Valentine's Day flowers from A. D. (via Gilet); carnival Veglione in black dominoes, Pierrot costumes; Pittsburgo falls in fountain.
- Mona Lisa visits, burns A. D.'s photo, threatens.
- Carlo's gardener's daughter; Polly and Boris "Sherlock and Watson" detective work.
- A. D. surprise party (sign "WELCOME, SURPRISE PARTY"); moonlit Coliseum.
- Pittsburgo suicide; American Embassy dinner (gold plates).
- Boris proposes; Polly wins a hat from Checkers (bet). Leaving Rome in March.
- Sorrento (olives, octopus at Naples, tarantella), Florence (Cascine, Boboli, Fiesole, photo beneath cypress), Venice (St. Mark's, gondola, sand-bar all night, Lido), Bayreuth (Wagner operas, Aunt hurries away), Baden-Baden, The Hague (House in the Woods; homesickness), London (Half Moon Street, Easthope), Leicestershire (Carlton Curlieu Hall, Kibworth; fox hunt; Oliver Cromwell's room; Duchess of Hamilton; Honorable Violet), Rome again; Frascati; Bracciano; Girandola fireworks; Teatro Costanzi fire at masked ball; Monte Catini (A. D. cure; Charlton ill).
- Telegram exchange Leicestershire vs Rome ("Can't you stand a little teasing?" ... "!" "." ).
- Gypsy fortune: "gray-eyed woman with a mysterious smile" trouble; "handsome man in the south" disappoint.
- Boris sends Polly "Bozhe moi" etc.; Boris tries to hold Polly in Paris room (wolf hound, growls; Sphinx at Luxembourg).

Part II: Court and Courting. A. D. and Polly letters in Sorrento/Florence/Venice; A. D. at Monte Catini; Admiral; Court Balls; Ambassador's Embassy ball; Boris's Russian letters; Polly's Black Horse Farm on the Hudson; engagement ring Christmas; Charlton dies (New Year's Day); A. D. resignation.

Part III: Uncertainty. A. D. cable "Will you marry me?" Polly: "Call it Heaven." Boris wants Polly; Polly in New York.

Part IV: The Prince in Pursuit.
- April 1: Polly cable "Breaking my engagement for reasons you can no doubt surmise." Next: "April Fool!" cable.
- Polly's Louisville Derby trip (Checkers and Sybil "trial hitch" engagement; Speed Limit won race; Mrs. Courtney's house; Boris falls from horse, scar).
- Camping trip Algonquin Park, Canada (Island Lake, Lake Kootchie, Big Smoke, Lake Bear, Lake Rod and Gun, Rock Lake; guides; canoe upset by Boris's hired guide; Boris kisses Polly in tent; "Kosloff" letters seen; "Bozhe moi").
- Customs officials on train: stolen old Masters; name "Kosloff."
- Polly's wedding plans, May 31 date, church, Rector; Aunt's acceptances; Boris threatens; bomb in parcel (set for one o'clock) dropped in pail of water by A. D.; Aunt elopes with Boris; Carpathia sailed 1:30; Checkers stops Aunt; Aunt returns.
- Conclusion (Anderson): unknown whether married; "Polly" lady found: letter "Dear Friend of Good Friday Night"; husband A. D. imprisoned in Russia; Boris in Moscow.
- Clipping in bag: Prince (German mother; forging; dictagraph; arrested; Polly's American lady). Anderson saw restaurant arrest of blue-eyed Slavic man and blonde woman on Good Friday week; Boris never seen again.

# BOOK 2 of 2: Dorcas Dene, Detective (George R. Sims)

Characters: **Dorcas Dene** (née Lester; lady detective; blonde, soft brown wavy hair, grey eyes; once actress, played old hag; narrator's friend); **Paul Dene** (blind artist husband; pipe; "Council of Four"); **Mrs. Lester** (mother; "Mrs. Lester"; dislikes melodrama); **Toddlekins** (brindle bulldog, saved a woman from drunken husband); **narrator Mr. Saxon** (dramatist, "assistant"); **Mr. Johnson** (retired superintendent of police, neighbour, first employer). Oak Tree Road, St. John's Wood. Dorcas's father an artist, Paris/Quartier Latin.

Stories:
1. **Council of Four** — Dorcas meets narrator at solicitor's (Mr. ----). Lord Helsham disappeared; mother Lady Helsham; Dorcas took case. Dorcas's backstory: Paul lost sight; Mr. Johnson recruited her at a guinea a day. Dorcas to find Nella Dalroy (actress, photo "To dearest Bertie, from Nella"; photographer Alfred Ellis, Baker Street; "The Gipsy Wife").
2. **Helsham Mystery** — Helsham clothes found near Cromer; real story: Lady Helsham substituted her premature baby daughter-for-son swap with sister (Mrs. ---- in Dunkeld, Scotland; captain in merchant service); Hon. John Farman heir; Lady Helsham's adopted daughter the real heir. Helsham hid as "nephew"; letter from Dunkeld; Dorcas persuaded Lord Helsham (the real one) to fake suicide.
3. **Man with the Wild Eyes** — Colonel Hargreaves (Orley Park, near Godalming); daughter Maud, found in lake with marks on throat; Dorcas nurses as trained nurse; "The Chequers" inn; lodge-keeper Peters, wife (Mrs. Peters); man with wild eyes peered at gate ~7pm; footprints; Dorcas found pointed-toed boot footprints; hat in lake.
4. **Secret of the Lake** — Victor Dubois (French master's son; husband, secret marriage 1891 at London; "V" scarf-pin; photo from album with erased name; London Stereoscopic Co. negative 111,492); insane; Maud's secret marriage; Dubois drowned; body found later by nurse rowing; Somerset House certificate; inquest verdict.
5. **Diamond Lizard** — Mrs. Charrington's jewellery (diamond and ruby bracelet, pendant, diamond lizard); stepson Claude Charrington (suspected); Miss Dolamore (actress, red tie with lizard pin) in Fitzroy Street with landlord Carlo Rinaldi and wife (former mistress of Mr. Charrington senior). Star and Garter Richmond (Karl waiter); Dorcas posed as American tourist / parlour-maid.
6. **Prick of a Pin** — Camorra club (Soho); Dorcas as German frau "Mrs. Goldschmidt" with waiter Guiseppe; brandy spilled on Rinaldi; pawnticket; tiny blood spot; Mr. Charrington senior replaced jewels after Rinaldi's blackmail; diamond poodle with ruby eyes exchanged.
7. **Mysterious Millionaire** — Lady Anna Barraclough (widow of first husband, brother Earl of Dashton); husband Judkins Barraclough (South American millionaire, bitten arm; bigamist suspicion); cab, rose leaves on Burton Crescent steps; night burglary with dark lantern & goloshes; keys from braces-chain via Lady Anna; empty house; hidden.
8. **Empty House** — Burton Crescent; Aleem Mohammed (Indian-looking accomplice, Indian costume, gold spectacles); cage in back room; woman (Marian Judkins, first wife, deserted by John Judkins; "Jack") drugged with chloral, fed brandy; clothes in cupboard; Inspector Stromberg (CID); Judkins arrested for attempted murder; wife rescued.
9. **Clothes in Cupboard** — Stromberg arrest; Barraclough: "Off with every rag."
10. **Haverstock Hill Murder** — Mrs. Hannaford (widow of Charles Drayson, died Paris Opéra Comique fire); husband Mr. Hannaford (stockjobber; Broadmoor); Inspector Swanage; Flash George at Kempton Park (Dorcas disguised as old gipsy woman selling race cards); £100 note 35421 from Drayson's 5,000 pound cheque at Union Bank; Dorcas's theory; Hannaford's door cracked.
11. **Brown Bear Lamp** — Bear with hidden slit; bank notes hidden; Flash George and Charles Drayson (alive; posed as old man with grey beard and Inverness cape); Hungerford Bridge; Thomas Holmes (partner, Italian organ-grinder disguise); Drayson jumped into Thames; Hannaford released; Dorcas: "These are the rewards of my profession."

Transcriber's note: underscores mark italics.
